grounded_facts: Paul Edgecomb wakes up to the sound of a clock radio broadcasting the morning weather.
A regular morning at Georgia Pines Nursing Home, marked by the clock radio's weather report and Paul waking up.
memories.memory_text: I woke up at Georgia Pines to the clock radio playing the morning weather, just like any other day.

grounded_facts: Paul arrives in the breakfast room and acknowledges Elaine Connolly, initiating social presence in the scene.
A group of retirees, including Elaine Connolly, are having breakfast together in the breakfast room.
memories.memory_text: I entered the breakfast room and saw Elaine Connolly sitting with a few other ladies, sipping tea while a group of retirees chatted around her.

grounded_facts: Paul gives Elaine a rakish wink in response to her good-morning smile, reinforcing their friendly bond.
memories.memory_text: I gave Elaine a rakish wink in return after she smiled at me, and it made her smile even more.

grounded_facts: Paul takes two pieces of leftover toast from the serving plate without permission.
memories.memory_text: I reached past the others and took two pieces of cold leftover toast from the serving plate without asking.

grounded_facts: Paul leaves the breakfast room after taking toast and exchanging a look with Elaine.
memories.memory_text: I exchanged a look with Elaine, gave her a silent 'catch ya later,' and then I left the breakfast room.

grounded_facts: Paul leaves the building through the back door without being seen, using a red rain poncho from the wall.
memories.memory_text: I slipped to the back door unnoticed, took a red rain poncho from the wall, and eased outside, making good my escape.

grounded_facts: Paul walks up the ridge toward the nursing home in the morning mist, arriving on foot after a walk through the wooded hills.
memories.memory_text: I walked up the ridge toward the nursing home through the morning mist, enjoying the quiet of my walk as I nibbled on a piece of toast I'd brought along.

grounded_facts: Brad Dolan scowls and mutters 'Old fuck' while looking up at Paul on the ridge.
memories.memory_text: I heard Brad Dolan mutter 'Old fuck' under his breath while looking up at me on the ridge.

grounded_facts: Brad Dolan, an orderly, arrives at the nursing home in a pickup truck and proceeds toward the building.
memories.memory_text: I saw Brad Dolan arrive in his pickup truck and head toward the nursing home, getting out and slamming the door behind him.

grounded_facts: Paul encounters a majestic buck in the woods, sharing a still, silent moment before the animal flees.
memories.memory_text: I was walking through the woods, munching on a piece of toast, when I heard a rustling and froze—I turned and saw a majestic buck not twenty feet away; we stood completely still, just watching each other in silence until it bounded off into the trees, and I let out a breath, shaking my head in wonder before continuing on.

grounded_facts: Paul discovers a pair of old wooden storage shacks along the path as he continues forward.
memories.memory_text: I moved forward after the encounter, took another bite of toast, and saw a pair of old wooden storage shacks ahead on the path.

grounded_facts: Paul returns from a walk in the woods during the day, arriving at the back door of the nursing home.
memories.memory_text: I returned from my walk in the woods and was reaching for the back door when Brad Dolan jumped out and grabbed me.

grounded_facts: Brad Dolan confronts Paul upon his return, accusing him of breaking rules by taking a staff poncho and questioning his activities in the woods, physically restraining him and inspecting his clenched hand.
memories.memory_text: I felt scared when Brad confronted me, accusing me of breaking rules by wearing a staff poncho and demanding to know what I was doing in the woods, questioning me like I was doing something wrong.

grounded_facts: Brad Dolan grabs Paul's wrist and later his other hand, forcing him to open it, causing pain and fear.
memories.memory_text: I cried out because Brad hurt me when he grabbed my wrist and then forced my other hand open, making me reveal the crushed toast I was hiding.

grounded_facts: Elaine appears and interrupts the confrontation, offering Paul tea and creating a moment of de-escalation.
Elaine steps out with tea, interrupting the confrontation and offering Paul comfort.
memories.memory_text: I remember Elaine stepping in just as things got tense, calling my name and bringing me tea, which broke the moment and gave me some relief.

grounded_facts: Dolan threatens Paul that if he reports the incident, he will be labeled as having senile delusions and not believed.
Dolan questions Paul's rule-breaking and implies he has no credibility, threatening to discredit him if he speaks up.
memories.memory_text: I remember Brad Dolan leaning in after releasing me and threatening that if I told anyone about what happened, he'd say I was having senile delusions and no one would believe me.

grounded_facts: When Elaine suggests reporting Brad, Paul resists, fearing escalation of abuse.
memories.memory_text: I resisted Elaine's suggestion to report Brad because I feared it would provoke him and make things worse for everyone.

grounded_facts: A group of elderly residents watch television together, initially viewing Jerry Springer before switching to a classic film.
memories.memory_text: I saw a group of residents watching television together, switching from Jerry Springer to a classic film with Fred and Ginger dancing.

grounded_facts: Paul sees the 'Cheek to Cheek' number from 'Top Hat' on TV and is overwhelmed by a flood of memories, leading to an emotional breakdown.
memories.memory_text: I saw the 'Cheek to Cheek' dance number from 'Top Hat' on TV, and suddenly I was overwhelmed by memories I couldn't control, and I burst into tears.

grounded_facts: Brad Dolan pretends to care about Paul's distress but is rebuffed by Elaine, revealing their antagonistic relationship.
memories.memory_text: I felt Brad Dolan's hand on my shoulder and heard him speak, pretending to care, but I knew it wasn't genuine concern—he was just trying to get under my skin.

grounded_facts: Elaine physically and verbally rejects Brad's false show of concern for Paul, asserting her protection of him.
memories.memory_text: I saw Elaine step in and shove his hand away, then tell him firmly that I didn't need his help, and in that moment, I felt protected despite my distress.

grounded_facts: Elaine deduces that the film reminded Paul of his past and presses gently for confirmation.
memories.memory_text: I remember Elaine looking at me and asking, 'Was it the film?' and then pressing gently with 'It was, wasn't it?' as if she could see right into my thoughts.

grounded_facts: Elaine reaches out and takes Paul's hand, affirming her friendship to encourage him to speak.
memories.memory_text: I felt her reach over and take my hand, a quiet gesture that told me she was there with me, ready to listen.

grounded_facts: A private, emotionally significant exchange between Paul and Elaine in which Paul begins to open up about his long-untold experiences from 1935.
memories.memory_text: I sat there, staring out the window, feeling the weight of 1935 return, and then I began to speak—telling her about the Green Mile and Old Sparky, the first time I’d shared that part of my life with anyone in years.

grounded_facts: Paul decides to speak about his past as a prison guard on death row, identifying 1935 as a defining year due to both personal suffering and the case of John Coffey and the two dead girls.
Paul discloses that he was in charge of death row and supervised executions, a fact previously unknown to Elaine.
memories.memory_text: I decided to finally speak with Elaine about my time as a prison guard during the Depression, telling her I was in charge of death row and supervised all the executions, something she didn’t know—I hadn’t spoken of these things in over sixty years, and 1935 stands out as the defining year, not just because of the worst urinary infection of my life, but because of John Coffey and the two dead girls.

grounded_facts: Paul Edgecomb experiences painful urination while on duty in the E Block toilet, showing physical distress.
memories.memory_text: I was in the E Block toilet trying to urinate, but it was so painful I could feel the sweat on my forehead and every bit of distress in my body.

grounded_facts: John Coffey, a massive new inmate, is brought to E Block in shackles by guards Percy and Harry; his arrival causes visible surprise due to his size.
memories.memory_text: I remember that John Coffey, a massive new inmate, is brought to E Block in shackles by guards Percy and Harry; his arrival causes visible surprise due to his size.

grounded_facts: Paul asks Coffey if he will cause trouble, assessing his potential threat level.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Paul asks Coffey if he will cause trouble, assessing his potential threat level.

grounded_facts: Paul silences Percy's disruptive 'dead man walking' chant and orders him off the block.
memories.memory_text: I told Percy to stop his disruptive chanting and ordered him off the block, making it clear I wouldn't tolerate his behavior any longer.

grounded_facts: Coffey politely clarifies the pronunciation and spelling of his name.
memories.memory_text: I remember Coffey politely clarifying to me that his name is pronounced like the drink, but spelled differently.

grounded_facts: Coffey reveals he is afraid of the dark in unfamiliar places and asks if a light remains on after bedtime, showing vulnerability.
memories.memory_text: I heard Coffey ask if we leave a light on after bedtime, and he told me he gets scared in the dark when it's a strange place, which struck me as a rare moment of vulnerability.

grounded_facts: Coffey unexpectedly extends his hand to Paul in a gesture of politeness, which Paul accepts, creating a moment of human connection.
memories.memory_text: I was surprised when Coffey offered me his hand like a gentleman, and though I hesitated, I took it—I felt an unexpected connection in that moment.

grounded_facts: After being settled, Coffey whispers to Paul that he couldn't help what happened and tried to stop it, implying guilt or trauma.
memories.memory_text: After being settled, I remember Coffey looking up at me and whispering that he couldn't help what happened and tried to stop it, and the softness in his voice made me wonder what he meant.

grounded_facts: The formal process of receiving and processing John Coffey into E Block, including his entry, cell assignment, and initial orientation.
memories.memory_text: I remember that The formal process of receiving and processing John Coffey into E Block, including his entry, cell assignment, and initial orientation.

grounded_facts: Paul orders Dean to take Delacroix to the infirmary to have his fingers examined after Percy's attack.
memories.memory_text: I told Dean to take Delacroix up to the infirmary to have his fingers checked after Percy attacked him.

grounded_facts: Percy verbally taunts and physically assaults Del after being reprimanded by Paul.
After being reprimanded, Percy retaliates by violently striking Delacroix's fingers with his baton, causing injury and distress.
memories.memory_text: I saw Percy lash out at Del after being reprimanded, striking his fingers with the baton and causing him real pain—I heard the crack and saw Del on his knees, crying out to me about his broken fingers.

grounded_facts: Paul begins reading Coffey's file while sitting alone on the bleachers, indicating a moment of private investigation or reflection.
memories.memory_text: I sat alone on the bleachers with Coffey's file on my knees, unwrapping my sandwich as I began to read through it, starting my own quiet look into his case.

grounded_facts: Klaus Detterick violently attacks Coffey in grief and rage upon seeing his daughters' bodies.
memories.memory_text: I saw Klaus Detterick rush down the riverbank and throw himself at John Coffey, screaming and hitting him in rage when he saw his daughters' bodies.

grounded_facts: Howie runs to his father and embraces him as they both break down in grief.
memories.memory_text: I watched Howie run to his father and cling to him as they both broke down in tears after the others pulled Klaus away from Coffey.

grounded_facts: McGee cautiously questions Coffey about his name and what happened.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed McGee cautiously question Coffey, asking him for his name and what had happened; I heard Coffey say, 'John Coffey. Like the drink, only not spelt the same,' and later respond with regret, 'I couldn't help it. I tried to take it back, but it was too late.'

grounded_facts: Warden Hal Moore reveals to Paul that his wife Melinda is suffering from worsening health symptoms, including severe headaches and hand weakness.
memories.memory_text: I remember Hal telling me that his wife Melinda was having severe headaches and weakness in her right hand, and that they were going to Indianola for tests because she was scared and so was he.

grounded_facts: Hal tells Paul he received a complaint about removing Percy from the block.
memories.memory_text: I recall Hal telling me he got an angry call from the state capital asking if it was true that I had ordered Percy Wetmore off the block.

grounded_facts: Paul confirms he ordered Percy Wetmore off the prison block due to his violent and reckless behavior.
memories.memory_text: I confirmed to Hal that I had ordered Percy off the block because of his violent behavior, including breaking three of Delacroix's fingers that morning out of petulance.

grounded_facts: Paul speculates that Percy wants to stay on the block to witness an execution firsthand.
memories.memory_text: I told Hal I thought Percy just wanted to stay on the block to see an execution up close, but I wasn't certain—I was only speculating.

grounded_facts: Paul is awake late at night, drinking buttermilk and listening to soft music, expressing concern about Melinda, Hal, and the new inmate.
memories.memory_text: I was up late at night, sitting at the kitchen table drinking buttermilk and listening to soft music on the radio.

grounded_facts: Paul reveals that a new inmate arrived—'a big, simple-minded fella'—and implies the case troubles him.
memories.memory_text: I mentioned to Janice that we got a new inmate today—a big, simple-minded fella—and I could tell just saying it out loud made me uneasy.

grounded_facts: Paul refuses to see Doc Sadler for his urinary issue, fearing side effects from sulfa tablets.
memories.memory_text: I told Janice I wouldn't see Doc Sadler about my urinary issue because I'm afraid the sulfa tablets would make me spend the whole week vomiting in every corner of my office—I'd rather let it run its course.

grounded_facts: An intimate late-night exchange between Paul and Janice in the kitchen, marked by emotional closeness and shared concern.
memories.memory_text: Janice came downstairs when she noticed I was awake, and we ended up talking quietly in the kitchen, sharing our worries—I even told her about my urinary issue and how I’d rather not take sulfa tablets because I know they’d make me sick.

grounded_facts: Janice strokes Paul's hair, sits on his lap, and kisses him above the eyebrow—a gesture that brings him comfort.
memories.memory_text: I remember Janice coming into the kitchen, stroking my hair, then sitting on my lap and giving me that crooked smile before kissing me above the left eyebrow—her special spot that always makes me prickle inside. She did it again later, and I couldn't help but smile.

grounded_facts: Jack Van Hay and a small crew, including Paul and Dean, perform maintenance on the electric chair 'Old Sparky' at night.
memories.memory_text: I was sanding a connector plug on Old Sparky during the night maintenance, working alongside Dean, who was waxing the chair's wooden arms, as part of the small crew led by Jack Van Hay.

grounded_facts: Brutal softly calls out to Paul and Dean from off-screen, interrupting their work and momentary pause after hearing a laugh.
memories.memory_text: I paused my work when I thought I heard a laugh from E Block, and just then Brutal softly called out to me and Dean, saying 'Paul? Dean?' from off-screen.

grounded_facts: Brutal directs Paul and Dean's attention to the mouse on the Mile.
memories.memory_text: Brutal pointed and told me to look again, making sure I saw the mouse on the Mile before I could fully process what was happening.

grounded_facts: Dean voices concern that the mouse might be rabid.
memories.memory_text: I heard Dean say he was worried the mouse might be rabid, since it wasn't acting like a normal mouse should around people.

grounded_facts: A small brown mouse emerges and walks along the Mile, drawing the attention of the guards.
Guards observe and react to the unexpected appearance of a mouse walking down the Mile.
memories.memory_text: I saw a small brown mouse walking down the Mile, checking the cells like it belonged there, and we all just stared at it in disbelief as it stopped and looked up at us.

grounded_facts: Brutal ignores Dean's objection and feeds the mouse anyway.
Brutal offers a piece of sandwich to the mouse, which eats it, confirming its tameness and curiosity.
memories.memory_text: I saw Brutal ignore Dean's protest and offer a piece of his sandwich to the mouse, which took it and ate right there, proving it wasn't afraid of us.

grounded_facts: The mouse disappears under the door of the restraint room, prompting concern about infestation.
memories.memory_text: I saw the mouse dart under the door of the restraint room, and Dean told me it would start chewing the padding to make a nest, which worried me.

grounded_facts: Paul instructs Dean to block the mouse from escaping during the search.
memories.memory_text: I told Dean to watch the door and hit the mouse if it tried to get past him.

grounded_facts: Dean asks whether he should hit the mouse or Brutal if someone tries to pass.
memories.memory_text: Dean asked me whether he should hit the mouse or Brutal if someone tried to pass.

grounded_facts: Guards conduct a full-scale search of the restraint room to capture the mouse.
memories.memory_text: I led the search to catch the mouse by unlocking the restraint room, handing Dean a mop, and moving heavy items out with Brutal to clear the space.

grounded_facts: Paul, Brutal, and Dean clear the restraint room of heavy objects to search for the mouse.
memories.memory_text: Brutal and I moved the heavy furniture and paint buckets out of the restraint room so we could search for the mouse, and Dean helped us clear the room.

grounded_facts: After failing to find the mouse, Paul accuses Dean of letting it escape.
memories.memory_text: After we couldn't find the mouse, I accused Dean of letting it get past him.

grounded_facts: Despite clearing the room, the guards fail to find the mouse, realizing it has outsmarted them.
memories.memory_text: We searched every corner of the empty room but still couldn't find the mouse, and I realized we had been outsmarted by it.

grounded_facts: Harry jokes that only E Block regulars can feed the mouse, implying Bill is just a floater.
memories.memory_text: I heard Harry joke that only E Block regulars could feed the mouse, implying Bill was just a floater when the mouse ignored him.

grounded_facts: The mouse enters the E Block and walks along the Green Mile toward Percy, drawing attention from the guards and inmates.
memories.memory_text: I noticed the mouse walking along the Green Mile toward Percy, and I could feel the tension building as everyone on the block watched it.

grounded_facts: Percy defiantly tells the guards they can 'kiss my ass' if they don't like his attitude.
memories.memory_text: I heard Percy defiantly tell the guards they could 'kiss my ass' if they didn't like his attitude.

grounded_facts: Paul warns Percy that threatening a man on the block will result in collective retaliation, regardless of job consequences.
memories.memory_text: I warned Percy that if he ever threatened a man on the block again, we'd all come after him—job consequences be damned.

grounded_facts: Paul confronts Percy about his aggressive behavior, warning him about the dangers of yelling and threatening others.
memories.memory_text: I confronted Percy about his aggressive behavior, making it clear that yelling and threatening others wouldn't be tolerated.

grounded_facts: Percy frantically searches the restraint room, throwing out furniture and belongings to find the mouse.
memories.memory_text: I saw Percy frantically searching the restraint room, throwing furniture and belongings everywhere in a wild attempt to find the mouse, and I told him to get all that mess cleaned up and back in place because he was cluttering up my Mile.

grounded_facts: A chaotic incident where Percy violently reacts to the mouse's presence, leading to a chase and confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Percy react violently when the mouse appeared, and I remember shouting at him to get everything back into the restraint room to restore order on my Mile.

grounded_facts: Paul notifies Bitterbuck that his daughter and her family have arrived for a visit.
memories.memory_text: I told Bitterbuck that his daughter and her family had arrived for a visit.

grounded_facts: A visit by Bitterbuck's daughter and her family to see him in prison.
memories.memory_text: I figured Bitterbuck’s daughter and her family were there to see him, though I didn’t see them myself.

grounded_facts: Bitterbuck is called out from his cell to meet his daughter and her family.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bitterbuck come out of his cell after I spoke to him, escorted by Bill Dodge, so his family must have been waiting.

grounded_facts: Paul orders the start of rehearsal preparations while Bitterbuck is away.
memories.memory_text: I ordered the rehearsal to start right away, wanting to get in at least two sessions before Bitterbuck returned.

grounded_facts: Paul controls when Toot may begin praying during the rehearsal, asserting authority over ritual timing.
memories.memory_text: I told Toot he had to wait for my signal before he could start praying, making it clear I was in charge of the ritual's timing.

grounded_facts: Harry physically interrupts Toot's loud prayer by slapping him, enforcing decorum.
memories.memory_text: I saw Harry slap Toot to stop his loud prayer, which enforced the decorum I was trying to maintain during the rehearsal.

grounded_facts: Paul announces that Reverend Schuster will conduct the actual execution ceremony, replacing any tribal or unconventional rites.
memories.memory_text: I announced that Reverend Schuster would be conducting the actual execution ceremony since Mr. Bitterbuck is a Christian, making it clear that no tribal or unconventional rites would take place.

grounded_facts: Toot delivers a crude and irreverent final statement during the rehearsal, mocking the execution process.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Toot deliver a mocking and crude final statement during the rehearsal, pretending to pray and then shouting about wanting a fried chicken dinner and making vulgar jokes, which broke the seriousness of the moment.

grounded_facts: Paul scolds Brutal and the team for losing control after Toot's joke, emphasizing the need for discipline.
memories.memory_text: I scolded Brutal and the team for losing control after Toot's joke, telling them to stay quiet and reminding them that we have a real execution tomorrow and can't afford to let laughter take hold.

grounded_facts: Van Hay instructs Percy on the function of the generator and the meaning of 'roll on one' and 'roll on two'.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Van Hay that 'roll on one' means he turns the generator up full, making the prison lights brighter in half the block.

grounded_facts: Van Hay explains the purpose of soaking the sponge in brine to conduct electricity during execution.
memories.memory_text: I learned from Van Hay that the sponge must be soaked in brine to conduct electricity directly to the brain quickly, like a bullet, and that we must never throw the switch without it.

grounded_facts: Toot-toot takes Bitterbuck's place in a mock execution rehearsal, simulating the condemned prisoner's role.
A full procedural rehearsal for Arlen Bitterbuck's execution, conducted with Toot-toot as the stand-in prisoner.
memories.memory_text: I oversaw the full rehearsal for Bitterbuck's execution, with Toot-toot taking his place on Old Sparky; I had to keep everyone focused and quiet, reminding them this was serious and we'd be doing it for real the next night.

grounded_facts: After Toot's inappropriate outburst and the mouse's appearance, Paul orders the rehearsal to be redone properly.
The mouse appears one day before the actual execution, observed during the rehearsal's conclusion.
memories.memory_text: I saw the mouse sitting on the door sill watching us, and after Toot's outburst and the team's laughter, I knew we couldn't let it slide—I told them to reset and do the rehearsal properly.

grounded_facts: Bitterbuck poses a philosophical question to Paul about whether sincere repentance could lead to reliving one's happiest time in the afterlife.
Bitterbuck wonders aloud whether sincere repentance could allow a person to return to their happiest moment and live there forever, suggesting a personal hope about the nature of heaven.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bitterbuck asking me if sincere repentance could let a person go back and live forever in their happiest moment, wondering if that’s what heaven might be like.

grounded_facts: Paul tells Bitterbuck he believes in the idea of returning to one's happiest time, though he does not truly believe it, in order to comfort him.
Paul tells Bitterbuck he believes in the idea of returning to one's happiest time after death, though he does not truly believe it, in order to comfort him.
memories.memory_text: I told Bitterbuck that I just about believe in the idea of returning to your happiest time after death, even though I didn’t truly believe it, because I wanted to comfort him.

grounded_facts: Bitterbuck recounts his happiest memory—his first summer with his young wife in the mountains—to Paul.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bitterbuck telling me about his first summer with his young wife in the mountains—he said it was his best time, and I could hear the warmth in his voice as he described making love every night and talking until sunrise.

grounded_facts: Brutal arrives at the cell door, checks his pocketwatch, and nods to Paul, indicating that it is time for Bitterbuck's execution.
Brutal silently communicates to Paul, via checking his watch and nodding, that it is time for Bitterbuck's execution to begin.
memories.memory_text: I saw Brutal arrive at the cell door, check his pocketwatch, and nod to me, letting me know it was time for Bitterbuck's execution to begin.

grounded_facts: Paul offers final words of reassurance to Bitterbuck, telling him it will be fine and that he will do fine.
Paul tells Bitterbuck that everything will be fine and that he will do fine, offering final encouragement before the execution.
memories.memory_text: I told Bitterbuck it would be fine and that he would do fine, offering him my reassurance before the execution.

grounded_facts: Paul and Brutal lock eyes in silent acknowledgment of the gravity and tension of the execution.
memories.memory_text: I locked eyes with Brutal, and in that silent moment, I knew he felt it too—the heavy weight of what we were doing and the tension hanging over the room.

grounded_facts: After the first application of current, Bitterbuck is found without a heartbeat but not definitively dead, prompting a second shock.
memories.memory_text: After the first shock, I saw Bitterbuck go limp, and when the doctor checked and shook his head, I realized he wasn't dead yet—so I knew we'd have to do it again.

grounded_facts: Brutal gives the order 'Roll on two' to initiate the first electric current.
The execution of Bitterbuck begins with the sponge being placed on his head and the current first applied.
A formal execution carried out in the prison's execution chamber using the electric chair.
memories.memory_text: I oversaw the execution of Bitterbuck in the chamber, watching as the sponge was placed on his head and the straps secured before Brutal gave the order to roll on two; I saw the current hit him and his body surge against the restraints, knowing this was the formal process we were bound to carry out.

grounded_facts: Brutal physically pushes Percy away after he mocks Bitterbuck's corpse.
memories.memory_text: I saw Brutal shove Percy away and heard him say, 'He's paid what he's owed. He's square with the house again, so keep your goddamn hands off him,' and I felt a surge of relief that someone had finally stood up to Percy's disrespect.

grounded_facts: Brutal covers Bitterbuck's face with a sheet and wheels the gurney away, asserting dignity over the corpse and rejecting Percy's mockery.
The immediate aftermath of an execution, where Bitterbuck's body is handled and removed from the tunnel.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bitterbuck's dead face on the gurney, how Brutal covered it with a sheet and wheeled him away down the tunnel, giving him the dignity Percy tried to steal.

grounded_facts: Paul tells Percy that he is always the problem, directly blaming him for the tension.
memories.memory_text: I told Percy, 'You, Percy. Always you,' because I couldn't keep ignoring how he's the source of all the tension between us.

grounded_facts: A tense exchange between Paul and Percy following the execution, involving personal conflict and professional demands.
memories.memory_text: I heard Percy ask me, 'What's up his ass?' and then challenge me directly, 'You gotta hate the new boy? That the way it is around here?'—as if I owed him some explanation, as if he wasn't the one making everything harder.

grounded_facts: Percy demands to take Brutal's role in the next execution, threatening to stay permanently if denied.
memories.memory_text: Percy demanded to take Brutal's spot in the next execution and told me, 'I wanna be out front, is all. Just one time. Then you'll be rid of me,' making it clear he saw this as a way to advance despite his incompetence.

grounded_facts: Percy implies he will remain indefinitely unless promoted, using institutional entrenchment as leverage.
memories.memory_text: I was told Percy might 'stick around for good, make me a career of this' if I didn't give in, which felt like a threat to entrench himself no matter what I decided.

grounded_facts: Paul expresses disgust at Percy's desire to participate in an execution and walks away without agreeing, signaling refusal.
memories.memory_text: I shook my head in disgust when Percy pushed for the execution role and just walked away, knowing I couldn't agree to something so wrong.

grounded_facts: The mouse, later named Mr. Jingles, is discovered by the guards in Delacroix's cell, where he is perched on Del's shoulder and performing simple tricks.
memories.memory_text: I saw the mouse sitting on Delacroix's shoulder when we arrived at his cell, and I watched it crawl over his head and along his arm like he was showing off a trick.

grounded_facts: Delacroix demonstrates the trained behaviors of the mouse, Mr. Jingles, including fetching a spool and performing tricks, in front of the guards on E Block.
Delacroix proudly shows off Mr. Jingles' ability to fetch the spool, seeking approval and admiration from Paul and the other guards.
memories.memory_text: I saw Delacroix put the mouse on the floor and toss a spool, and I watched it roll the spool back to him just like he said it would, and I could tell he was proud when he asked us to watch it again.

grounded_facts: Upon Percy's arrival, Delacroix becomes fearful and begs Percy not to harm the mouse.
memories.memory_text: I saw Del become afraid and beg Percy not to hurt the mouse when he arrived.

grounded_facts: Paul asks Percy if this is the same mouse he previously chased, confirming identity and seeking input on keeping it.
memories.memory_text: I asked Percy if this was the same mouse he had chased before, and I brought up Del's idea of keeping it in a box as a pet to see what he thought.

grounded_facts: Delacroix reveals that the mouse's name is Mr. Jingles, claiming the mouse whispered it in his ear, and requests a box so the mouse can sleep with him.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Delacroix that the mouse's name is Mr. Jingles, that it whispered the name in his ear, and he asked me for a box so the mouse could sleep with him.

grounded_facts: Contrary to his usual cruel demeanor, Percy unexpectedly approves of giving Delacroix a cigar box lined with cotton to house the mouse.
memories.memory_text: I was surprised when Percy, instead of being cruel, agreed to let us get a cigar box lined with cotton for the mouse to live in.

grounded_facts: A private meeting between Hal and Paul in Hal's office during the day, initiated by Hal to deliver urgent personal and professional news.
memories.memory_text: I entered Hal's office during the day and found him staring out the window; when I asked if he wanted to see me, he told me to close the door, starting a private meeting.

grounded_facts: Paul threatens to have Billy sent to the padded room if he doesn't stop singing a disrespectful song about Delacroix.
memories.memory_text: I told Billy he was ten seconds away from spending the rest of his life in the padded room if he didn't stop singing that disrespectful song about Delacroix.

grounded_facts: Paul attempts to understand what Coffey means when he says he 'could feel it from here,' referring to Delacroix's death.
memories.memory_text: I tried to understand what Coffey meant when he said he 'could feel it from here,' so I asked him if he had heard it, but his cryptic response left me uncertain and I realized I wouldn't get a clear answer.

grounded_facts: Coffey expresses deep sorrow over Delacroix's execution, showing emotional exhaustion and implying he sensed the event psychically.
memories.memory_text: I saw Coffey grieving deeply over Delacroix's death, saying 'Poor Del. Poor old Del,' and later murmuring that Del was the lucky one now, which showed me how emotionally exhausted he was and made me wonder if he had sensed the execution happening somehow.

grounded_facts: Coffey indicates that Mr. Jingles has run off and likely will not return, marking a shift in the presence of the mouse as a symbolic and narrative element.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Coffey that Mr. Jingles had run off and likely wouldn't come back.

grounded_facts: Paul enters his house in the dark and goes to the kitchen, indicating a return to his residence after being away.
memories.memory_text: I came into my house in the dark, hung up my hat, and made my way to the kitchen, turning the radio on as I went.

grounded_facts: Paul prepares and sips a drink at the kitchen table, suggesting emotional or physical fatigue.
memories.memory_text: I poured myself a drink at the kitchen table and took a sip, feeling the weight of the day settle over me.

grounded_facts: Jan approaches Paul and holds him, responding to his emotional burden with comfort.
Jan silently responds to Paul's emotional state by holding him, offering solace without words.
memories.memory_text: I felt Jan come to me, fold my head into her arms, and hold me without saying a word, as I drew strength from her while the music played on.

grounded_facts: Paul and Jan arrive at Hal's house and wait at the front door, with Jan holding a baking dish, indicating a visit with purpose.
memories.memory_text: I stood with Jan at Hal's front door, and I noticed she was holding a baking dish, like we were supposed to be bringing something comforting.

grounded_facts: Paul expresses his discomfort about the situation, indicating emotional resistance.
memories.memory_text: I told Jan, 'I hate this,' because I couldn't hide how uncomfortable I felt about coming to Hal's house.

grounded_facts: Jan responds to Paul's expressed discomfort with simple acknowledgment.
memories.memory_text: Jan said 'I know' in response to me saying I hated the situation, and her simple reply felt like she understood without needing more.

grounded_facts: A visit by Paul and Jan to Hal's house in the morning, likely intended as a gesture of support.
memories.memory_text: I think we came to Hal's house in the morning to offer some kind of support, though I wasn't sure it helped, especially when he opened the door and let us in.

grounded_facts: Paul observes Melinda Moore's frail and deteriorated appearance due to cancer, which shocks him, though he attempts to conceal his reaction.
memories.memory_text: I was shocked by how frail and worn down Melinda appeared because of the cancer, and though I tried to hide it, the sight of her nearly broke me.

grounded_facts: A morning visit by Paul, Jan, and Hal to Melinda Moore, who is sitting outside in the sun, frail from cancer.
memories.memory_text: I arrived with Jan and Hal to visit Melinda one morning, seeing her sitting outside in the sun, frail from cancer, and I could feel the weight of how sick she looked.

grounded_facts: Jan warmly greets Melinda by smiling, kissing her, and holding her hands, providing emotional comfort and shielding Paul's reaction.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jan immediately comfort Melinda with a warm smile, a kiss, and by holding her hands, shielding me from having to hide my reaction any longer.

grounded_facts: Paul gives Jan a meaningful look that conveys his deep emotional dependence on her.
memories.memory_text: I gave Jan a look that said everything—how much I depended on her in that moment, how I didn’t know what I’d do without her.

grounded_facts: Hal explains to Paul that on bad days, Melinda exhibits uncharacteristic behavior, including involuntary swearing with no awareness.
Hal tells Paul about Melinda's uncharacteristic swearing during bad days, expressing both sorrow and relief that she is having a good day.
memories.memory_text: I remember Hal telling me that on bad days, Melinda isn't herself—she swears in her sweet voice, awful words she doesn't even know she's saying, and he spoke with such sorrow, yet he was relieved that day because she was having a good one.

grounded_facts: Paul verbally expresses his love and emotional dependence on Jan.
Paul tells Jan that he loves her and cannot imagine life without her, revealing emotional vulnerability.
memories.memory_text: I told Jan that I love her and I don't know what I'd do if she were gone, because I truly can't imagine my life without her.

grounded_facts: Paul proposes a plan to have the boys over, seeking Jan's implicit approval.
An upcoming social gathering where Paul intends to host the boys.
Paul suggests having the boys over the next day, introducing a new plan.
memories.memory_text: I proposed having the boys over the next day and asked for Jan's approval, sharing my plan to bring them together.

grounded_facts: Paul discloses that John Coffey healed him of a bladder infection, establishing Coffey's supernatural healing power as a credible phenomenon.
memories.memory_text: I told the others that John Coffey healed me of my bladder infection by placing his hands on me, and I could see they were stunned by what I said.

grounded_facts: Paul appeals to Brutal's sense of justice and compassion to gain support for taking Coffey to Melinda.
memories.memory_text: I told Brutal that what's happening to Melinda is an offense to the eyes, the ears, and the heart, and I acknowledged it was a lot to ask of him since he doesn't know her like I do.

grounded_facts: Paul implies and the group begins to consider taking John Coffey to Melinda Moores for healing, despite the extreme risks.
memories.memory_text: I suggested there might be a chance to take John Coffey to Melinda Moores for healing, even though I knew it meant risking our jobs or worse—I could see the fear in the others, especially Harry, who didn't want to consider it at all.

grounded_facts: Harry opposes the plan by emphasizing the danger of Coffey escaping and the moral burden of potential harm.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Harry that he opposed the plan because Coffey is a murderer and he feared what would happen if he escaped—I heard him say he'd hate losing his job or going to prison, but he'd hate having a dead child on his conscience even more.

grounded_facts: A domestic meal shared by Paul, Jan, Brutal, Dean, and Harry, during which a serious moral and logistical discussion unfolds.
memories.memory_text: I shared a meal with Jan, Brutal, Dean, and Harry, and during it, I spoke up about Coffey's innocence and how I didn't think he had committed the murders, even as Harry expressed his fears about the risks we'd face if Coffey escaped.

grounded_facts: Paul directly contradicts the accepted narrative of Coffey's guilt, introducing moral ambiguity.
Paul states he does not believe John Coffey murdered the children, challenging the foundational assumption of Coffey's imprisonment.
memories.memory_text: I told the others I don't think Coffey did it at all, and I just can't believe God would give such a gift to a man who would kill a child.

grounded_facts: Paul crushes morphine pills into powder on a stainless steel gurney, and Brutus carefully transfers the powder onto a small sheet of paper.
memories.memory_text: I crushed the morphine pills into powder on the stainless steel gurney, and I saw Brutus carefully transfer the powder onto a small sheet of paper.

grounded_facts: Paul withholds the cola and demands Billy promise to behave before allowing him to drink.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Paul withholds the cola and demands Billy promise to behave before allowing him to drink.

grounded_facts: Paul prepares a cola drink laced with morphine and gives it to Billy after securing his promise to behave, marking the beginning of the execution plan.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Paul prepares a cola drink laced with morphine and gives it to Billy after securing his promise to behave, marking the beginning of the execution plan.

grounded_facts: Coffey quietly agrees to participate in the execution, shocking the guards.
Coffey quietly agrees to participate in the execution plan when asked indirectly.
memories.memory_text: I heard Coffey quietly agree to take part in the execution when I asked, saying he'd like to take a ride, and I saw the others turn to stare at him in shock.

grounded_facts: Percy's possession of a 'Tijuana Bible' is revealed when his book falls, exposing the hidden pornographic material.
memories.memory_text: I saw Percy's book fall to the floor and realized it was hiding a 'Tijuana Bible'—a crude pornographic comic with Olive Oyl and Popeye in a compromising position.

grounded_facts: Brutal ridicules Percy upon discovering the 'Tijuana Bible', undermining his dignity.
memories.memory_text: I heard Brutal mock Percy, saying 'Oooo, Poicy! What would your mother say?' right after the Bible was exposed.

grounded_facts: Brutal applies pain and threatens to mutilate Percy's ears to force compliance.
memories.memory_text: I saw Brutal twist Percy's ears and threaten to rip them off if he didn't comply, and Percy screamed in pain and fear.

grounded_facts: Percy, now restrained, begs Paul not to place him in the cell with Wild Bill.
After being restrained, Percy begs Paul not to place him in the cell with Wild Bill, revealing fear and vulnerability.
memories.memory_text: I remember Percy, now restrained, begging me not to put him in the cell with Wild Bill—he sounded afraid, almost broken, pleading with me directly.

grounded_facts: Percy is physically overpowered and forced into a canvas straitjacket by Paul, Brutal, and Harry.
memories.memory_text: I helped Brutal and Harry overpower Percy and force him into a straitjacket when he tried to run, shoving him hard once it was on.

grounded_facts: A punitive and humiliating intervention carried out by Paul, Brutal, and Harry to subdue Percy in Paul's office.
memories.memory_text: I was part of the intervention in my office where Brutal, Harry, and I subdued Percy, forced him into a straitjacket, and I gave him a hard shove to assert control.

grounded_facts: After Percy's plea, Paul responds with a forceful shove, expressing anger and rejection.
memories.memory_text: After he begged, I gave him a hard, angry shove—I couldn't bring myself to show him any mercy after everything he'd done.

grounded_facts: Brutal mocks Percy with a crude joke about Olive Oyl while locking him in the restraint room.
memories.memory_text: I saw Brutal mock Percy with that crude joke about Olive Oyl while we were locking him in the restraint room.

grounded_facts: Paul silences Percy by slapping tape over his mouth and shoving him into the restraint room.
Percy is disarmed, gagged with tape, and locked in the restraint room by the guards as punishment for his actions toward Del.
memories.memory_text: I stepped forward with the strapping tape, slapped it over Percy's mouth, and shoved him into the restraint room while Brutal took his holster and baton; we slammed the door shut and I told him he'd have a few hours of quiet time to reflect on what he did to Del.

grounded_facts: The guards unlock the gun safe, retrieve shotguns, and load them before proceeding down the Mile.
memories.memory_text: I helped unlock the gun safe, took out the shotguns, and loaded mine before we headed down the Mile together.

grounded_facts: Coffey is unlocked from his cell and brought out to be moved, as part of a covert prison operation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Coffey's cell being unlocked and watched him emerge, so I motioned for the team to move out, making sure everything stayed on track for the operation.

grounded_facts: A coordinated effort by the guards to secretly move Coffey while concealing their actions by framing noise on Percy and fabricating alibis.
memories.memory_text: I was part of the coordinated effort to secretly move Coffey, using the noise from the restraint room as cover and setting up alibis—Dean was told to say I was in Admin going over Del's file while the others had their own cover stories.

grounded_facts: Billy grabs Coffey's wrist and slurs a threatening question, initiating a disturbing physical and emotional reaction.
Billy suddenly grabs Coffey's wrist, triggering a strong, fearful reaction in Coffey as if experiencing a supernatural connection.
memories.memory_text: I saw Billy suddenly reach out and grab Coffey's wrist, and I watched Coffey tremble in horror as if something terrible passed between them, like an electric shock, while Billy slurred a threatening question.

grounded_facts: Coffey verbally identifies Billy as a 'bad man' twice, indicating deep moral revulsion and fear.
memories.memory_text: I heard Coffey say twice that Billy was a 'bad man,' his voice filled with fear and revulsion, as if he sensed something deeply evil in him.

grounded_facts: Coffey reacts with horror upon seeing the electric chair, claiming that fragments of executed souls remain within it and can be heard screaming.
Coffey is brought into the execution chamber, indicating a procedural movement likely related to an upcoming execution or routine transfer.
memories.memory_text: I saw Coffey being brought into the execution chamber and freeze in horror at the sight of Old Sparky, then heard him say, 'They're still in there. Pieces of them, still in there. I hear them screaming,' revealing his belief that fragments of executed souls remain within the chair.

grounded_facts: Paul urgently instructs Coffey to stop resisting and proceed toward the door.
memories.memory_text: I urgently told John to come along and move toward the door, and I saw him finally respond by pulling away.

grounded_facts: Paul instructs Coffey to lie on the gurney to make passage easier.
memories.memory_text: I told Coffey to lie down on the gurney because it would be easier for him to move through the tunnel and no harder for us.

grounded_facts: Coffey lies down on the gurney to make it easier to traverse the tunnel due to his height.
memories.memory_text: I saw Coffey lie down on the gurney on his back, making it easier for him to go through the low tunnel because of his height.

grounded_facts: Coffey begins to smile and touch the tunnel walls as he is pushed along, expressing enjoyment.
Coffey smiles and says the ride is fun.
memories.memory_text: I saw Coffey start to smile as he was pushed along the tunnel, reaching out to touch the walls with his fingertips, and then he said to me, 'Say. This is fun,' letting me know he was actually enjoying the ride.

grounded_facts: Coffey is brought up from the tunnel beneath the prison wall and emerges into the night outside.
memories.memory_text: I helped bring Coffey up from the tunnel beneath the prison wall, and we emerged into the night together.

grounded_facts: A coordinated escape from the prison through a tunnel and side gate under cover of night.
memories.memory_text: I inferred we were carrying out a coordinated escape through the tunnel and side gate under cover of night, though I didn't know every detail.

grounded_facts: Coffey excitedly points out the constellation Cassie, shaped like a lady in a rocking chair, sharing his wonder with Paul.
memories.memory_text: I saw Coffey gaze up at the stars with wonder and point excitedly, telling me, 'Look, boss! It's Cassie, the lady in the rocking chair!'

grounded_facts: Paul tells Coffey to be quiet to avoid detection during the escape.
memories.memory_text: I told Coffey to be quiet because we couldn't risk being heard during the escape.

grounded_facts: Brutal tells Coffey they see the lady in the stars to comfort him after Paul silences him.
memories.memory_text: I saw Brutal tell Coffey they saw the lady in the stars too, to comfort him after I silenced him.

grounded_facts: The group exits through a rarely used iron gate in the prison wall, beginning their escape across the fields.
memories.memory_text: I saw the group exit through a rarely used iron gate in the prison wall, and we began our escape across the fields under cover of night.

grounded_facts: Coffey misreads the guards' anxious looks and offers them leaves to smell, which they accept to appease him.
memories.memory_text: I noticed the guards looked anxious, and when Coffey misread it, he offered us leaves to smell, so I took them to keep him calm and happy.

grounded_facts: A nighttime journey through the woods during which the guards escort Coffey to a hidden truck, uncover it, and prepare for vehicular travel.
The guards lead Coffey to a thicket where they remove branches to reveal a concealed old truck, preparing for the next stage of travel.
memories.memory_text: I was there in the woods at night when we led Coffey to a thicket and started clearing branches to uncover a battered old Farmall truck hidden in the brush, getting ready to shift from walking to using the vehicle.

grounded_facts: Coffey notices fireflies gathering around him playfully, interprets it as a sign of mutual affection, and shares this moment with the guards, who observe in awe and unease.
memories.memory_text: I saw Coffey laugh and play with fireflies gathering around his hand, speaking to them like old friends, and I watched in awe and unease as he seemed completely at peace in a moment both magical and unsettling.

grounded_facts: Coffey explains to Paul that the fireflies are drawn to him because he loves them and they feel no hurtful thoughts, only happiness.
memories.memory_text: Coffey told me the fireflies came to him because he loved them and they felt no hurtful thoughts—just happiness—and I remember how sincerely he believed it.

grounded_facts: Harry gives Paul a look asking if they can leave, expressing discomfort with the surreal firefly scene.
memories.memory_text: Harry gave me a look asking if we could leave, and I could see he was uncomfortable with how strange the whole firefly scene had become.

grounded_facts: Coffey climbs onto the back of the truck, followed by Paul and Brutal, marking the transition from walking to vehicular movement.
memories.memory_text: I urged Coffey to board the truck, and I saw him climb onto the back before I joined him with Brutal, marking our shift from walking to driving away.

grounded_facts: When asked if he knows where they are going, Coffey responds that they are going to help a lady, showing unexplained awareness of their purpose.
memories.memory_text: I asked Coffey if he knew where we were taking him, and he said, 'Help a lady?'—which was right, but when I pressed him on how he knew, he just said he didn't know much about anything. It struck me as strange that he could know something so specific while claiming to understand so little.

grounded_facts: Brutal expresses fear and urges Paul to turn back before approaching the house.
memories.memory_text: Brutal told me we could still turn back, and I heard the fear in his voice before we approached the house.

grounded_facts: An urgent nighttime visit by Paul, Brutal, and Coffey to the Moore household to provide help during a crisis.
memories.memory_text: I was part of an urgent trip with Brutal and Coffey to the Moore house that night to help during a crisis.

grounded_facts: The group arrives at the Moore house in the truck, with headlights illuminating the isolated property at night.
memories.memory_text: I saw our truck's headlights cut through the dark as we arrived at the Moore house, illuminating the isolated property.

grounded_facts: Hal confronts Paul and Brutal at gunpoint, demanding to know their intentions and suspecting a prison break.
memories.memory_text: I heard Hal shout from the doorway, demanding to know who was there, and I could see the gun in his hands—I told him to take his finger off the trigger because I knew he thought we were part of some prison break.

grounded_facts: Melinda shouts from upstairs, cursing and demanding that the visitors be sent away, revealing her deteriorated mental state.
memories.memory_text: I heard Melinda shouting from upstairs, cursing at us, and I realized how bad her condition had become when she called Hal a fucking cocksucker.

grounded_facts: Coffey's presence has a hypnotic, calming effect on Hal, causing him to lower his guard and become mentally unfocused.
memories.memory_text: I noticed how Coffey's presence seemed to calm Hal down, making him less focused and more compliant, almost like he was under a spell.

grounded_facts: Coffey gently takes the shotgun from Hal's hands, removing immediate threat and asserting control.
Coffey moves past Hal into the house, marking the beginning of his intervention.
memories.memory_text: I saw Coffey gently take the shotgun from Hal's hands and then pass by him into the house, stepping in to handle the situation with Melinda.

grounded_facts: Paul tells Melinda that her X-ray was clear and there was no tumor.
memories.memory_text: I told Melinda that her X-ray was clear and there was no tumor, seeing the relief in her eyes.

grounded_facts: After healing Melinda, Coffey collapses into violent coughing fits, showing severe physical distress and requiring support from Brutal and Paul.
memories.memory_text: I saw Coffey collapse into violent coughing after healing Melinda, barely able to breathe, and I watched Brutal rush to support him as he struggled to get up.

grounded_facts: Melinda tells Coffey she dreamed of him, expressing a deep spiritual connection.
memories.memory_text: I heard Melinda tell Coffey that she dreamed of him, that they found each other in the dark, and I could see the weight of those words between them.

grounded_facts: After being healed, Melinda regains full cognitive function, recalls recent events, and walks unaided to Coffey.
memories.memory_text: I saw Melinda regain her clarity, remember her dream, and walk unaided to Coffey, touching his face as she spoke to him.

grounded_facts: Melinda gives Coffey her necklace of St. Christopher as a token of gratitude and protection.
memories.memory_text: I saw Melinda give Coffey her St. Christopher necklace, and when she asked him to wear it so the saint would keep him safe, I nodded to let him know it was all right.

grounded_facts: Coffey performs a supernatural act of healing, drawing illness from Melinda Moores through a kiss, restoring her to full health while visibly suffering the effects himself.
Coffey gently instructs Melinda to remain still before initiating the healing.
A supernatural healing event takes place at Melinda Moores' bedside, involving Coffey, her husband Hal, and Paul's group, resulting in her full recovery and Coffey's physical collapse.
memories.memory_text: I watched Coffey heal Melinda Moores right before my eyes—he kissed her and drew the illness out, restoring her completely while he collapsed from the sickness himself, and I saw him tell her to stay still before it began.

grounded_facts: Brutal privately tells Paul that Coffey will die soon, implying suicide, and that he won't be executed.
Brutal states that Coffey will die soon, likely by suicide, before reaching execution.
memories.memory_text: I remember Brutal pulling me aside and telling me that Coffey wouldn't be executed—he said he'd be dead soon, likely by his own hand, and that one of us would find him dead on his bunk within days.

grounded_facts: Coffey is physically assisted from Moore's house to the truck's stakebed due to extreme physical weakness.
memories.memory_text: I helped Coffey out of Moore's house and toward the truck because he was so weak—he could barely stand—and then we got him up onto the stakebed, where Harry covered him with a blanket; I said we should get him back on the Mile.

grounded_facts: A titled narrative segment marking Coffey's return to the prison block, symbolizing the final phase of his story.
memories.memory_text: I think Coffey’s return to the Mile marks the final phase of his story, though I didn’t say it outright—I told Brutal that if Coffey chooses to die soon, he’s earned that right.

grounded_facts: Paul decides to take Coffey back to the prison block known as the Mile.
memories.memory_text: I decided we should take Coffey back to the prison block, and I said, 'Let's get him back on the Mile.'

grounded_facts: Paul slaps Percy and threatens him with physical harm and social exposure unless he remains silent about the events involving Del's execution.
memories.memory_text: I slapped Percy hard and told him he'd be beaten within an inch of his life if he didn't stay silent about what happened with Del's execution, and I made sure he knew we could expose his cowardice to everyone.

grounded_facts: After being released from the straitjacket and regaining his belongings, Percy is seized by Coffey, undergoes a supernatural transfer, and then mindlessly shoots Wild Bill six times in the chest.
memories.memory_text: After Dean brought back Percy's belongings, I watched him smooth his hair, put on his hat, and start strapping on his holster—then Coffey lunged through the bars, seized him, and performed a horrifying transfer, their mouths forced together as dark essence flowed into Percy, his baton clattering to the floor, his body jerking helplessly before he was released, vacant and broken, only to walk mindlessly to Wild Bill's cell and shoot him six times in the chest.

grounded_facts: The guards confront Percy in the restraint room after leaving Coffey, threaten him into silence, and later witness his transformation and violent actions on the Mile.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Percy being grabbed by Coffey, saw the strange black things enter him, and later watched him act vacant and violent on the Mile until we tackled him and took his gun, then saw the black things leave him and turn white.

grounded_facts: Coffey pleads with Paul to take his hand and forcibly shares a vision of Wild Bill's crime, revealing the truth about the twins' murder.
Coffey compels Paul to hold his hand, forcing him to witness a detailed vision of Wild Bill murdering the Detterick twins, confirming Coffey's innocence and the true nature of the crime.
memories.memory_text: I remember Coffey pleading with me to take his hand, and then I couldn't resist—I had to reach out, and when we touched, I was pulled into a vision of the Detterick twins playing in the dust, their mother calling them in, and then the horror of seeing Wild Bill drag them away; I felt it all as if it were happening to me, and I knew in that moment that Coffey was innocent.

grounded_facts: Coffey forcibly transfers the black 'insects' (evil essence) from himself into Percy, healing himself but driving Percy into a catatonic state, then reveals Wild Bill's guilt by sharing a vision of the crime with Paul.
memories.memory_text: I saw Coffey grab Percy through the bars and force something dark from himself into Percy’s mouth and nose—black things like insects swirling in the air—while lightbulbs exploded around us; I snapped my fingers at Percy afterward but he didn’t respond, just walked blankly up the Mile and shot Wild Bill six times; then Coffey told me he saw the truth in Wild Bill’s heart, and when I took his hand, I felt a surge and saw the Detterick twins laughing in the sun, playing hopscotch before they died, and I knew Wild Bill had killed them.

grounded_facts: Law enforcement conducts an on-site investigation following a violent incident, collecting statements and evidence from guards and staff.
memories.memory_text: I was there when the cops arrived and started questioning Percy, trying to get him to respond, and I heard Dean and Harry talking about how he just snapped, with Brutal mentioning how Wild Bill had scared him days before.

grounded_facts: Percy is found handcuffed and unresponsive on the Mile, being examined by a medic who suggests severe mental impairment.
A medic examines Percy and concludes he is mentally incapacitated.
memories.memory_text: I saw Percy sitting handcuffed on the floor of the Mile, his eyes completely blank, and when the medic checked him with a penlight and got no response, he said Percy's cheese had slid off his cracker—I knew then he was mentally gone.

grounded_facts: Hal privately confronts Paul, demanding to know if the events at his house are connected to the prison incident, showing distrust and urgency.
Hal promises to protect Paul, even at the cost of his job, in exchange for truth about the incident at Hal's house.
memories.memory_text: Hal pulled me aside and demanded to know if what happened at his house was connected to the prison, and he told me he’d cover for me, even if it cost him his job, just as long as I gave him the truth.

grounded_facts: Paul lies to Hal, denying any connection between the prison events and the incident at Hal's house.
memories.memory_text: I looked Hal in the eye and told him no, even though I knew there was a connection—I chose to lie to protect the secret.

grounded_facts: Paul informs the group that Wharton worked at the Detterick farm, establishing a factual link between Wharton and the victims.
Paul discloses having read the file and confirms that Wild Bill Wharton was hired at the Detterick farm in the spring to repair the barn, establishing his connection to the victims' family.
memories.memory_text: I told the others that I had read the file and confirmed Wharton was hired by the girls' father last spring to repair the barn, which established his connection to the victims before he came back and took them.

grounded_facts: Jan suggests fabricating a confession by Wharton to stop Coffey's execution, with Brutal backing it up to explain Percy's actions.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Jan that we should say Wharton confessed to the crime, and that Brutal could back it up to explain why Percy shot him, but I couldn't go along with lying like that.

grounded_facts: Jan shifts from legal solutions to demanding direct action, urging the guards to help Coffey escape permanently.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jan telling me that since we had proof Wild Bill was at the Detterick farm, we had to stop Coffey's execution and get him a new trial, and when that didn't work, she demanded I help Coffey escape on my own.

grounded_facts: The guards collectively reject Jan's escape proposal, citing Coffey's size, recognizability, and the inevitable consequences for their careers and families.
memories.memory_text: I spoke up and told Jan there was no way Coffey could escape without being caught quickly—he's too big and noticeable—and I knew it would destroy us and our families if we tried.

grounded_facts: Frustrated and heartbroken, Jan denounces the guards as murderers and cowards for refusing to act to save Coffey.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jan shout at us, calling the guards cowards and murderers for not stopping Coffey's execution, her voice breaking with anger and pain.

grounded_facts: Jan directly accuses Paul of becoming a murderer if he proceeds with Coffey's execution, equating him morally with Wharton.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jan pulling away from me, screaming that if I carry out the execution, I'll be a murderer just like Wharton, and the look in her eyes told me she meant it.

grounded_facts: After her proposals are rejected, Jan insists that the guards orchestrate a fake escape for John Coffey.
memories.memory_text: After I rejected her idea, Jan kept pushing, telling me to fake Coffey's escape like we'd done before, and when I refused, she called me a coward and said I'd be no better than Wharton if I let the execution go forward.

grounded_facts: A group conversation at Paul's house at dusk where Jan, Paul, and the guards debate Wharton's role in the Detterick girls' murders and possible actions to save Coffey.
memories.memory_text: I was there at my house at dusk when Jan, I, and the guards debated whether Wharton could be the real killer and whether we could stop Coffey's execution, but when I tried to comfort Jan, she pulled away and ran off crying.

grounded_facts: Jan apologizes to Paul for previously calling him a coward, expressing deep regret.
memories.memory_text: Jan told me she was deeply sorry for calling me a coward and said she felt worse about it than anything else she'd ever said to me in our marriage.

grounded_facts: Paul agrees with Jan's insistence not to tell Hal about Coffey's innocence, making a binding decision.
memories.memory_text: I agreed with Jan when she insisted I shouldn't tell Hal about Coffey's innocence because he couldn't help, and I promised her I wouldn't.

grounded_facts: Paul confesses to Jan that he feels in real danger of hell for the first time, indicating deep moral crisis.
memories.memory_text: I told Jan for the first time that I feel in real danger of hell, because I've done things I'm not proud of and this guilt is different.

grounded_facts: An intimate late-night exchange between Paul and Jan in the kitchen, marked by emotional vulnerability and serious discussion.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting at the kitchen table late at night, sipping my beer, when Jan came down looking miserable and exhausted; she apologized deeply for calling me a coward, saying she felt worse about it than anything she'd ever said to me in our marriage. I told her no, that I've been thinking about it too, and honestly, I've done things I'm not proud of, but this is the first time I've ever felt in real danger of hell.

grounded_facts: Jan touches Paul's face and urges him to talk to John Coffey to find out what he wants.
memories.memory_text: Jan touched my face and told me to talk to John Coffey, to find out what he wants, and I remember how urgently she said it.

grounded_facts: Coffey expresses his desire for a specific last meal before execution, indicating acceptance of his fate.
memories.memory_text: I asked Coffey what he'd like for his last meal, and he said he'd enjoy meatloaf, mashed potatoes with gravy, and maybe some okra, which showed me he was accepting what was coming.

grounded_facts: Coffey refuses the offer of a preacher but invites Paul to pray with him, signaling trust and emotional intimacy.
memories.memory_text: I offered Coffey a preacher, but he said he didn't want one—instead, he invited me to pray with him, and when I asked if he meant me, he said he could kneel with me if it came to that, which made me feel he trusted me deeply.

grounded_facts: Paul and the guards visit Coffey to discuss final arrangements before his execution.
memories.memory_text: I entered Coffey's cell with the guards to discuss his final arrangements, asking him about his last meal and whether he wanted a preacher.

grounded_facts: Paul questions the morality of the execution and suggests letting Coffey escape, testing his own conscience.
memories.memory_text: I asked John what he wanted me to do, if he wanted me to let him escape, because I couldn't shake the feeling that executing him might be wrong.

grounded_facts: Coffey comforts Paul by framing the execution as an act of kindness, alleviating Paul's moral burden.
memories.memory_text: I remember John taking my hand and telling me to stop worrying, that I should see his execution as a kindness because he wanted it over.

grounded_facts: Coffey reveals his deep emotional and psychic exhaustion, affirming his wish for execution as a release.
memories.memory_text: I heard John say he was tired—tired of the pain in the world, tired of being lonely—and in that moment, I understood how much he just wanted relief.

grounded_facts: Coffey shares that he has never seen a motion picture, leading to a poignant moment of human longing.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Coffey that he had never seen a motion picture, and it struck me how such a simple thing meant so much to him.

grounded_facts: A late-night film screening in the prison auditorium featuring a Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers movie, attended by Paul and other inmates.
memories.memory_text: I was in the prison auditorium late at night, watching a movie with the other men.

grounded_facts: Coffey is deeply moved and astonished by the dance performance of Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers, interpreting them as angels from heaven.
Coffey softly expresses his belief that Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers are angels from heaven due to the beauty of their dance.
memories.memory_text: I saw how deeply moved Coffey was by the dance of Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers, and I heard him softly say they were angels from heaven.

grounded_facts: Coffey reassures the guards that he will be all right, attempting to ease their emotional burden.
memories.memory_text: I remember Coffey stepping out and looking at us, seeing how sad we all were, and then he told us, 'I be all right, fellas. This here's the hard part. I be all right in a little while,' trying to comfort us even as he faced death.

grounded_facts: Paul temporarily takes custody of Coffey's religious medal before the execution.
memories.memory_text: I asked John for his St. Christopher medal just before the execution, telling him I'd give it back after, and he let me take it.

grounded_facts: Coffey recounts a dream in which Mr. Jingles brings joy to children, including the murdered Detterick girls, in a peaceful afterlife setting.
memories.memory_text: I listened as John told me about his dream, where Mr. Jingles brought joy to children in a peaceful place, and I heard him say the Detterick girls were there, laughing and unharmed, sitting on his knees.

grounded_facts: Brutal urges Coffey to feel the love from those who don't hate him, offering emotional support.
memories.memory_text: I saw Brutal step in and tell Coffey to feel the love from those who didn't hate him, trying to offer some comfort in the middle of all that anger.

grounded_facts: Marjorie verbally attacks Coffey, wishing him prolonged suffering.
memories.memory_text: I heard Marjorie Detterick curse at Coffey, screaming for him to die slow and calling him a baby-killer, her voice full of hate as we prepared for the execution.

grounded_facts: Coffey, Paul, Dean, Brutal, and Harry kneel together in prayer before the execution.
memories.memory_text: I was there with Brutal, Harry, and Dean when Coffey knelt down to pray, and though I felt uncertain, I joined him; then Dean knelt too, and after a pause, Brutal and Harry followed, and together we all knelt in prayer before the execution.

grounded_facts: Coffey pleads not to have the mask placed over his face, revealing his fear of the dark.
memories.memory_text: I remember Coffey looking at me with terrified eyes and pleading, 'Please, boss, don't put that thing over my face,' begging me not to put him in the dark because he was afraid.

grounded_facts: During Coffey's prayer, Paul experiences a vision of the Detterick sisters praying, mirroring Coffey's words.
memories.memory_text: While Coffey prayed, I saw a vision of the Detterick girls kneeling together on their porch, saying the same words he spoke—'be my strength, be my friend'—and in that moment, I felt their innocence and faith as clearly as if I had been there that night.

grounded_facts: Paul hears Coffey's final mental message about love being used as a weapon in the world.
memories.memory_text: I heard the last thought in Coffey's mind as we held hands—how people kill with love, every day all over the world.

grounded_facts: Paul, after hesitation, gives the order to execute Coffey, completing his duty.
memories.memory_text: I hesitated, but then I gave the order to roll on two, because it was my duty to see it done.

grounded_facts: Coffey passively complies with the execution team, showing awareness and emotional preparation for death.
memories.memory_text: I saw how Coffey struggled as we brought him to the chair, heard him say he could feel the hate like bees stinging, and when he begged me not to put the hood over his face because he was afraid of the dark, I knew he was fully aware of what was happening and facing it with a quiet courage.

grounded_facts: The formal execution of John Coffey at Cold Mountain Penitentiary, carried out on the Green Mile.
memories.memory_text: I was there, carrying out the execution of John Coffey on the Green Mile—I spoke the formal words, gave the order, and watched it through to the end, fulfilling my duty even though it broke me.

grounded_facts: Coffey is electrocuted and dies, with visible signs of peace and tears at the end.
memories.memory_text: I watched Coffey die in the chair, his body jerking at first, then going still with a peaceful face and tears on his cheeks.

grounded_facts: Paul carefully replaces the St. Christopher's medal around Coffey's neck.
memories.memory_text: I carefully placed the St. Christopher's medal back around Coffey's neck.

grounded_facts: They wheel Coffey down the access tunnel.
memories.memory_text: I saw them wheel Coffey down the access tunnel.

grounded_facts: Paul is driving home at night, emotionally numb.
memories.memory_text: I drive home at night, my heart numb, feeling nothing as I grip the wheel of my Model T.

memories.memory_text: I pulled into the driveway and sat for a moment before going inside, and when I got out, Jan came out to meet me on the stairs.

grounded_facts: Jan steps out and takes Paul into her arms, providing comfort as he begins to sob.
memories.memory_text: She stepped forward and took me into her arms, holding me as I started to sob.

grounded_facts: Paul emotionally collapses and begins sobbing against Jan upon returning home, indicating a significant emotional release.
memories.memory_text: I couldn't hold it in anymore—I broke down against her, finally letting myself cry.
